newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins up on Yeltsin op news,track Vnesh.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins up on Yeltsin op news,track Vnesh.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose on Wednesday on news that President Boris Yeltsin is likely to be operated on in 6-8 weeks and dealers said firming Vnesh debt was another encouraging factor.
Cardiologists decided on Wednesday that Yeltsin should undergo heart surgery but they set no date for the operation. They said it would take 6-8 weeks to prepare Yeltsin for it.
At the weekend one leading cardiologist suggested Yeltsin might not be operated on at all.
The Yeltsin news dominated market talk, and operators largely ignored Tuesday's decision by the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee not to raise interest rates.
Dealers said foreign operators had been selling in early trading, while their local counterparties were mainly buying. Then the market stopped for breath for the time of doctors' meeting.

"Buying resumed when it was said the operation will take place. It is a positive factor as it is at least some official information and the operation is expected to be successful," an International Moscow Bank dealer said.
Dealers said MinFin bonds were following the rise in Vnesh debt.
"Selling (of MinFins) stopped when Vnesh debt firmed. London operators are likely to close their earlier short positions on the news about the operation," Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said.
Dealers said the 2008 maturity was most actively traded today.
